findings.text: The fallback guards on record.get("process_alive") is not False, a field the fleet read no longer populates, so a run whose local process has just died now reaches the guard as None and the sprint row reads live true where the pre-repair tree read live false — measured with one fixture against both arms, the fleet read handing on None at the head and False at the base, and the guard landed two days after the write it depends on.

The sentence says consumers derive liveness each under its own host gate, but record_process_alive takes a bare local probe and reckon/crew/directory.py:69 writes that probe into process_alive for every pointer, so a foreign run's pid number held here passes as the run's liveness: measured at the head, the directory row reads process_alive true with is_dispatching true when the recorded start tick matches the local holder, and reads unreadable with is_dispatching false when the recorded tick is the worker's own, which is the ordinary case.
